about:
Rig table. Every value carries its source: 'measured' (a reference surface, inverted through AgX), 'derived'
(computed from measured values, formula given) or 'decided' (a choice, reason given). Units: three.js intensity at toneMappingExposure 1.0; radiance = albedo x E / pi.

day_exterior_shade.what: same concrete inside the dish shadow, t059

day_interior.what: bedroom plaster out of the lamp pool (plaster-t069-b), t069 Day 1 11:50 (native)

planning_t035.what: kitchen wall tiles, t035 (planning phase, countdown 03:28, time of day unknown)

night_lamps_wall.what: bedroom plaster at night, 0.95-2.1 m from the lamp (lamp-t033 patches), t033 (native)

day_exterior_frame.what: frame median, t059 (native), for the dawn/day ratio

night_exterior_punchin.what: frame median, t036 (HUD-less punch-in; not used for the standard)

unusable.t013: blackout frame has a flat floor p1 33.7 = p5 33.9: a screen-space darkness overlay, not scene light; not an anchor

cct_k.source: decided: highlights of the native day frames read 6000-6030 K (t059, t032) and the sun sits a little warmer than the sky

elevation_deg.source: decided: short soft shadows in t059; not triangulated

azimuth_deg.source: provisional: slat shadows upper-left to lower-right in t049 (punch-in)

cct_k.source: decided: blue sky opposite a low sun

E_horizontal.source: derived: day sky x the same ratio

interior_DUSK_set_E.source: derived: the ss_04 anchor minus the LAMPS share 0.040 (the bed lamp is on in ss_04; upper bound from t033; P0-08 replaces it with the baked LAMPS value at that texel)

interior_with_lamps_E.source: measured: dusk_interior anchor (ss_04 17:20, bed lamp on)

interior_light.about:
Colour of the dusk interior light from ss_04 (17:20) against t069 (11:50): same materials, same home. The
per-channel scene ratio dusk/day, times the day interior light colour as rigged (86.9 % 5500 K sun bounce +
13.1 % 7500 K sky), gives the ss_04 light; removing the bed lamp's share (2700 K) gives the lamp-free DUSK set
colour, which is then split into the dusk sun (2600 K) and sky (8000 K) by least squares on chromaticity.
interior_light.dusk_set_label: measured light, CCT 6900 K (slightly off the blackbody curve; a 6900 K blackbody is #f6f4ff)

cct_k.source: decided: native night frames read 5440-5530 K overall with warm lamps in them (t033, ss_05)

azimuth_deg.source: decided: same as the day sun

E_normal.source: derived: 70 % (decided) of the native night exterior level (ss_05 frame median) on the moon

interior_NIGHT_set_E.source: measured (frame statistic): unlit corners of t033

interior_with_lamps_E.source: measured: t033 plaster wall 0.95-2.1 m from the lamp

I.source: derived: geometric mean of the per-patch estimates (working below)

cct_k.source: decided: warm bulb; the shade displays #daa850 (t069, lamps.json emitter_hex) via the emitter layer

geometry.value: bulb 0.95 m above the floor (table) or 1.5 m (floor lamp); decay 2; distance 6 m

calibration_target.source: measured anchor (t033); the bare point light at I from t069 fails it, so shades are required (decided)

geometry.value: SpotLight at 1.9 m, aimed 35 deg down, angle 50 deg, penumbra 0.6, decay 2, distance 8 m

geometry.value: SpotLight held at 1.3 m, aimed 35 deg down, angle 22 deg, penumbra 0.35, decay 2, distance 10 m

azimuth_deg.source: decided: same as the day sun

night_interior_E.source: decided: the NIGHT set (rain does not change the interior level)

day_interior_E.source: decided: equal to the overcast cold-wave interior (no native daytime storm frame)

sky_cct_k.source: decided: ss_05 mean 5530 K includes warm windows; overcast sky slightly cool

lightning.value: DirectionalLight 8000 K, E 3.0, 80-150 ms, 1-3 flickers every 8-20 s
lightning.source: decided: no lightning in the references

sky_cct_k.source: measured: t041 mean 6020 K, highlights 6320 K

hemisphere_fallback.about:
HemisphereLight fallback for movables without a probe. Sky and ground colours are normalised to unit
luminance (linear sRGB), so a vertical face (mean of sky and ground) receives exactly `intensity` = the rig's
vertical target E.

day.note: set with Color.setRGB(r, g, b, THREE.LinearSRGBColorSpace)

dusk.note: set with Color.setRGB(r, g, b, THREE.LinearSRGBColorSpace)

night.note: set with Color.setRGB(r, g, b, THREE.LinearSRGBColorSpace); add LAMPS where on

fog.about:
FogExp2 colour as scene-linear radiance: sky colour (linear, max 1) x E_h x 0.5 / pi, i.e. the radiance of a
50 % grey card under the sky; density reasons as fog fractions at the look point (10.47 m) and the far floor
edge at 60 deg (38.6 m along the ray).
fog.clear_weather: none (decided: no distance haze across the roofs in t059 or ss_06)
fog.density_reason: decided: storm 0.012 per m keeps the look point clear (1.6 %) and greys the far floor edge (19 %); cold wave 0.008 is two-thirds of that (0.7 % / 9 %) because snow haze is thinner than rain

bloom_emissive.source: decided: 2700 K emissive luminance 0.518 x 3.0 = 1.55, 1.55x the bloom threshold 1.0, so shades bloom and diffuse surfaces (at most 0.64 in day sun) do not

exterior_E_horizontal.source: decided: the measured cold-wave level (t041 tiles under the open cutaway) stands for the overcast sky

set.value: OVERCAST: uniform overcast sky dome + its bounce, no sun, normalised to 1.0 in the reference room
set.source: decided: overcast rigs must not reuse the DAY sun-bounce pattern

movables.about:
Movable objects (probe-lit): vertical-surface irradiance target in the day interior, and the display codes a
material then shows. The day-interior anchor itself is a vertical wall (plaster-t069-b), so E 0.419 is a
vertical-surface irradiance.

hair.albedo_from: hair_relative (k_up_1.25; dark cap core relative to the t069 hoodie)
hair.note: cap faces up: E 0.419 x k_up; the rim-lit per-frame values stay in character_measured.items.hair
